sentences.text: The holotype specimen, which serves as the primary reference for the species, preserves numerous vertebrae, ribs, shoulder and hip bones, along with a single tooth.
This animal is distinguished by unique anatomical features, including a crest on the front of its dorsal ribs and rugose surfaces on its scapula.
Researchers estimate that this giant could have reached a total length of 27 meters and a weight of 35 tons.
If its neck was held vertically, the head could have been positioned up to 16 meters above the ground, making it one of the tallest known dinosaurs in Europe.
Remains were first discovered in 2003 at the El Oterillo II locality in the Castrillo de la Reina Formation of Burgos, Spain.
The genus was formally described in 2017 by a team led by Fidel Torcida Fernández-Baldor and colleagues.
Currently, only one fossil occurrence of this taxon has been recorded in the scientific database.
Europatitan is classified within the dinosaur class Saurischia.
It belongs to the clade Somphospondyli, a group of titanosaurs.
The genus is generally classified as a member of Titanosauriformes and is sometimes placed within Somphospondyli.
Other analyses have corroborated a close evolutionary relationship between Europatitan and the genus Tastavinsaurus.
The type species of the genus Europatitan is Europatitan eastwoodi.
Europatitan lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 125 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
Specifically, it inhabited the Barremian to Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
The presence of Europatitan in Europe may reflect an exchange of vertebrate faunas between Gondwana and Laurasia at the beginning of the Cretaceous.
